title: Agentrys Shows You How to Build a Multi-Agent System in 30 Minutes - Semiwiki
gist: Agentrys is using Hot Chips 2026 and a September webinar to showcase its Studio Platform, claiming a multi-agent system given only a processor design and goal autonomously explored thousands of parameters and produced designs that beat expert-tuned references on timing while cutting power 2-5x, using open-source EDA tools.

insights.claim: Agentrys demonstrated a multi-agent system that, given only a processor design and a goal with no human tuning, explored thousands of design parameters and drove candidates to tool-verified silicon metrics using an entirely open-source EDA flow.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: If reproducible, this is evidence agentic AI can now autonomously run full physical-design optimization loops on open-source EDA, a capability gap that previously required large expert teams; worth scrutinizing for independent verification.
insights.quote: Working autonomously, the agents explored thousands of design parameters, rewrote the hardware itself, and drove every candidate all the way to real, tool-verified silicon metrics — using an entirely open-source EDA flow.
insights.locator: What Agentrys did was give a multi-agent system

insights.claim: Agentrys claims its autonomously generated chip designs hit a timing target that the original expert-tuned reference designs could not reach, while cutting power by 2-5x for select industrial workloads and reducing area.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A 2-5x power reduction claim versus expert-tuned baselines, if verified independently, would be a material data point for how far agentic design-space exploration can outperform human engineers on power, performance and area metrics.
insights.quote: The results were buildable designs that hit a timing target the original expert-tuned references couldn’t reach — while cutting power by 2–5X for select industrial workloads and trimming a significant amount of area.

insights.claim: Agentrys positions its Studio Platform as enabling teams to build an initial agentic AI chip-design flow in about 30 minutes, versus competitors' offerings that require long onboarding to customize pre-built flows or building a flow from scratch.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Speed-to-first-flow (30 minutes versus quarter-long projects) is Agentrys' core competitive claim versus incumbent agentic EDA offerings, a metric to test against rival vendors' onboarding time.
insights.quote: Agentrys believes that a purpose-built multi-agent system for chip design shouldn’t be a quarter-long project.

insights.claim: Agentrys describes its platform as enabling 'automatic evolution,' where deployed multi-agent chip-design systems adapt themselves to new data and new tasks after deployment, rather than requiring re-engineering.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Self-adapting agent systems, if real, reduce the maintenance burden of agentic EDA tooling over time, a differentiator to track versus static agent-flow vendors.
insights.locator: Automatic evolution: how Agentrys multi-agent systems adapt themselves

insights.claim: Agentrys' webinar and Hot Chips demo emphasize an end-to-end specification-to-GDSII multi-agent flow built on open-source EDA tooling that customers can then customize for internal flows, scripts, and proprietary data.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Open-source EDA-tool dependence, rather than proprietary big-three EDA suites, could lower the cost barrier for smaller design teams to adopt agentic design automation.
